markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the endorsement occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If Donald Trump publicly endorses Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 Brazilian presidential election before Oct 26, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An "endorsement" requires:
A clear, affirmative statement of support for candidate's election
The statement must be public (not private communications)
The endorsement must specifically reference the 2026 Brazilian presidential election or be clearly in context of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election
The endorsement must come directly from Donald Trump or through official channels

The following scenarios would resolve to YES:
Donald Trump states "I endorse candidate for [office]"
Donald Trump states "I support candidate" with clear reference to the 2026 Brazilian presidential election
Donald Trump states "I'm voting for candidate" publicly
Donald Trump states "candidate has my full support" for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election
Donald Trump appears at campaign events specifically to endorse
Donald Trump releases official endorsement through their organization
Donald Trump allows their name/image to be used in candidate's campaign materials

Statements of obvious sarcasm (or which are immediately followed by clarifications that Donald Trump is joking) are NOT encompassed by the Payout Criterion.

The Contract shall resolve immediately upon confirmation of the first qualifying endorsement in the specified race. If multiple candidates are listed for a listed race and exactly one is endorsed, that candidate's strike resolves "Yes" at $1.00 and all other named-candidate strikes resolve "No." If multiple are endorsed, each endorsed candidate's strike resolves "Yes" at a value of ($1.00 / N) rounded down to the nearest $0.01. 

If no endorsement occurs before expiration, the "No one" strike resolves "Yes" at $1.00 and all named-candidate strikes resolve "No."

If a candidate withdraws from, suspends their campaign for, ceases to be a candidate in, or loses the primary or general election for the specified race before a qualifying endorsement is confirmed, their strike may resolve to No in the sole discretion of the Exchange.
markets.title: Will Donald Trump endorse Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 Brazilian presidential election before Oct 26, 2026?

markets.rules_secondary:
Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law.

Standard legislation requiring executive approval: final passage by all required legislative bodies, executive signature OR becoming law despite executive inaction OR successful veto override, and satisfaction of any required waiting periods
Legislation not requiring executive approval: final passage and completion of required waiting periods
Constitutional amendments: passage with required supermajorities and completion of ratification processes
Executive orders: official signature, publication in official government records, and legal effectiveness

The following do NOT constitute enactment:

Legislative passage without completed executive action
Passage by only some required bodies
Provisional passage
Non-binding resolutions
Draft orders

Enactment occurs when all requirements are completed, regardless of pending judicial challenges.

The margin of victory is the vote share received by Darline Graham minus the vote share received by the candidate that finishes immediately behind Darline Graham if Darline Graham wins, or the candidate that finishes first if Darline Graham loses. If Darline Graham wins, the margin will be positive; if Darline Graham loses, the margin will be negative; if Darline Graham ties for first place, the margin shall be 0.

Each margin range is inclusive of its lower bound and exclusive of its upper bound, and no rounding shall be applied. For example, for consecutive ranges of 5-6% and 6-7%, a margin of 5.99999% resolves within the 5-6% range, while a margin of exactly 6% resolves within the 6-7% range. If Darline Graham runs under multiple parties or is listed multiple times, votes attributable to the same underlying candidate will be summed.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the law is enacted
markets.rules_primary: If AB 2512 (2025–26 Reg. Sess.), the Home Run for Anaheim Act, or any other measure imposing its requirement that Angel Stadium disposition materials identify the franchise as the "Anaheim Angels" is enacted in California before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law.

Standard legislation requiring executive approval: final passage by all required legislative bodies, executive signature OR becoming law despite executive inaction OR successful veto override, and satisfaction of any required waiting periods
Legislation not requiring executive approval: final passage and completion of required waiting periods
Constitutional amendments: passage with required supermajorities and completion of ratification processes
Executive orders: official signature, publication in official government records, and legal effectiveness

The following do NOT constitute enactment:

Legislative passage without completed executive action
Passage by only some required bodies
Provisional passage
Non-binding resolutions
Draft orders

Enactment occurs when all requirements are completed, regardless of pending judicial challenges.
markets.subtitle: :: California
markets.title: Will the Anaheim Angels naming bill become law?

markets.rules_secondary: A concession requires the candidate to explicitly acknowledge defeat, loss, or that their opponent has won the race. markets.rules_primary: If Taylor Hanson is officially announced to perform as an official contestant in Dancing with the Stars Season 35 before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For the purposes of this Contract, Taylor Hanson satisfies the Payout Criterion if either:

Official Announcement:
Taylor Hanson is officially announced, confirmed, or publicly credited as cast to perform an official contestant in Dancing with the Stars Season 35, regardless of whether the performance ultimately occurs; OR

Actual Performance:
Taylor Hanson appears on stage, on screen, or in recorded content as an official contestant in any official performance, showing, or release of Dancing with the Stars Season 35.

Additional clarification(s):

If Dancing with the Stars Season 35 is entirely cancelled or abandoned before any official performance or release occurs, but Taylor Hanson was officially announced in an official contestant, the Contract will resolve to “Yes.”

If multiple people are announced for an official contestant (e.g., alternating cast, dual casting), and Taylor Hanson is among them, the Contract will resolve to “Yes.” b

The Contract may resolve to “No” prior to the Expiration Date if:
(a) Dancing with the Stars Season 35 is cancelled or completes its run without Taylor Hanson being announced or performing in an official contestant, or
(b) another person is officially announced as the sole exclusive performer for an official contestant.
